title: Weighted Dip
summary: A bodyweight press on parallel bars, adding weight once bodyweight reps get easy, for the lower chest and triceps.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: dip bars or power tower; dip belt; weight plates or dumbbells or kettlebells.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.8 for chest (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.8 for triceps (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly triceps total.
Library rating 0.5 for front delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly front delts total.

setup.text: Support yourself on the bars with your arms straight, adding a belt or dumbbell if needed.
Lean your torso forward slightly to work the chest more.
Lower until your shoulders are a little below your elbows, or as low as feels comfortable.
Press back up to straight arms.

form_cues.cue: Lower until shoulders are just below elbows
Stop the descent at a depth your shoulders handle comfortably, and add depth over time.

mistakes.text: Swinging the legs to kick the weight up.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
